cells.tense: You hold many possible feelings at once and you can still pick among them.
cells.ask: Write down the two pulls you feel strongest about, then circle one and keep only that one in view for a week. Notice what the other costs you to set down.
cells.core:
A reach of feeling comes off you when you walk in — people feel pulled toward you before anyone says anything. Part of the power is that you leave room. You gather what might be felt and you hand back the choice, so the person feels met instead of steered. What good looks like here is that your draw and how you see do not fight; you want something specific and you see the whole thing it sits in, so nothing gets run over to get it.

That is the part worth treating as yours. You can keep a pull while keeping your distance from it, which most people can't do — they get ruled by whatever leans on them. Keeping this means continuing to hold the room open long enough that people choose you or don't, and continuing to say which one you wanted. Feed how you see next, not the pull.
cells.sheetLine: You leave real room for people to choose you, and you say what you wanted.
cells.verb: Gathering every feeling that might be had, and choosing among them.
cells.place: Where you stand outside the pattern you are inside, seeing what is true across it.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a moment ahead that hasn't happened yet and can't be fully written in.
cells.ask: Pick the one scene ahead that you keep rehearsing, say out loud that the ending is not written yet, and sit with the rehearsing and no plan for ten minutes.
cells.core:
You have run ahead into how it will feel and who will land where. From that vantage you keep the pull switched on so nothing is missed — every angle gets touched, every person gets a read, and behind all of it is three or four scenes you have already played through past the ending. None of that is reach anymore. It is management, and it costs the same as the draw.

The pattern you see is real, and it has stopped being a place you stand. Now it is a script you are standing in. Pull your face closer to right now — inside the room, across the table, in the ordinary afternoon — and the bracing will not survive the crowding. Let the ending stay unwritten and stay in the room anyway. That is the whole of it.
cells.sheetLine: You're managing what hasn't happened, and it costs the same as the draw.
cells.verb: Gathering every feeling that might be had, and choosing among them.
cells.place: Where you stand outside the pattern you are inside, seeing what is true across it.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you a while back.
cells.ask: Pick one half-formed feeling you keep circling and write it down in plain words — one page, tonight. Then read it and put it away.
cells.core:
The images come and you don't let them land. Feeling arrives in hints, half-finished, and before any of it can gather into an arc you step outside and look at it from a distance — a habit that once kept you safe and now keeps you from entering. What you have is a long list of almost-feelings and no whole one to stand in.

That kind of looking is not broken. It is doing what it was built to do — and doing it to everything, including your own life. Pick one thing that has been circling, put it in front of yourself in plain words, and let it stay there long enough to have a middle. The outside view will still be there when you come back.
cells.sheetLine: You see everything from outside, and you let nothing all the way in.
cells.verb: Gathering every feeling that might be had, and choosing among them.
cells.place: Where you stand outside the pattern you are inside, seeing what is true across it.

cells.tense: You are holding the pen in a room you're already writing, and you haven't said so.
cells.ask: Name one choice you have already made and keep describing as still open. Say it to one person as yours, plainly, before the week ends.
cells.core:
You know which one you picked. Some part of you registers a slight tinge whenever the subject surfaces, and still you offer it as undecided, still open, still under review. You chose already. The words for it haven't left your mouth. What reads as uncertainty to anyone watching is a very specific preference under a long guard.

When the pull runs clean, it honors both people: the reach stays and the pick gets said, so no one is fused and no one is left guessing. The pull isn't what needs treating. The paperwork does. State the pick and the pull can carry something real and specific in it. The reluctance to sign is the thing doing the damage now.
cells.sheetLine: You've already chosen, and someone else is still waiting for the decision.
cells.verb: Gathering every feeling that might be had, and choosing among them.
cells.place: Where you stand outside the pattern you are inside, seeing what is true across it.

attempts.check: The record supports the pull toward gathering emotional possibility and the outside-the-system view; it does not support anything about who is on the other end of that pull or what happened the last time they chose. A reader could reasonably say the pull is not emotional for them but practical — that what looks like many options is just a busy week. The ask survives this: naming the two strongest pulls in plain words in one sitting still teaches what the choosing feels like, and nothing about the mechanism depends on my read being right. The sentence that serves me more than them would be anything about an altered 'quiet knowing' — it flatters the map instead of pointing at a next act, so it is out.
